title: Find All Possible Recipes from Given Supplies
statement:
There are `n` recipes. Recipe `i` is called `recipes[i]`, and you can cook it once you hold every item named in `ingredients[i]`. At the start you hold every item listed in `supplies`, each in unlimited quantity.

- An ingredient may be the name of another recipe. After that recipe has been cooked, it counts as an item you hold, again without limit.
- An ingredient that is neither in `supplies` nor the name of a recipe you can cook is never available.
- Recipes may need each other (directly or through a longer loop); then none of the recipes in that loop can be cooked.

Return the names of every recipe you are able to cook, in any order (an empty list if there are none).
constraints: All names contain only lowercase English letters
The names in recipes and supplies are all different from each other
No ingredients[i] lists the same item twice
signature: List<String> findAllRecipes(String[] recipes, List<List<String>> ingredients, String[] supplies)
notes:
## Intuition

Think of every recipe as a task that waits on its ingredients. Supplies are ready from the start, so only ingredients that are not supplies make a recipe wait. Count those for each recipe: a recipe with a count of zero can be cooked right away, and cooking it may bring other recipes' counts down. This is Kahn's topological sort. Recipes stuck in a loop, or waiting on an item nobody can produce, never reach zero and are left out automatically.

A simpler idea is to sweep over all recipes again and again, cooking whatever is ready, until a sweep changes nothing. That is correct but can take O(n) sweeps.

## Approach

1. Put `supplies` in a set `available`.
2. For each recipe `i` and each `item` it needs that is not available, add one to `missing[i]` and record `i` in `needers` under `item`.
3. Put every recipe with `missing[i] === 0` in `queue`.
4. Take recipes from `queue` in order: add the name to `made`, then for every recipe in `needers` under that name, lower its `missing` count and enqueue it when the count hits zero.
5. Return `made`.

## Example 1, step by step

`available` is `{yeast, flour, corn}`. Both ingredients of `bread` are available, so `missing = [0]` and `needers` stays empty. `queue = [0]`; taking index 0 adds `"bread"` to `made`, nobody waits on bread, and the answer is `["bread"]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + S + I), where I is the total number of ingredient entries: each entry is examined once when counting and once when its recipe is cooked.
- Space: O(n + S + I) for the set, the counts and the `needers` lists.

## Pitfalls

- Count only ingredients that are not supplies; an item that is neither a supply nor a recipe must keep the count above zero forever, which this does for free.
- Do not recurse naively from recipe to ingredient recipe: two recipes that need each other would loop forever.
- Supplies come in unlimited quantity, so one item can satisfy many recipes; never "use up" anything.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `available` | the starting supplies |
| `missing[i]` | how many non-supply ingredients recipe `i` still waits for |
| `needers` | for each non-supply item, the recipes that need it |
| `queue`, `head` | recipes ready to cook, and the position of the next one to take |
| `made` | names of the recipes cooked so far, the answer |
